deep.reconstruction:
This page has no derivations, formulas or computations. It belongs to Hilbert's notebook of aphorisms and methodological remarks, continuing the previous page (the Frege postcard on axioms as implicit definitions) and leading into the next (problem choice, D'Alembert). Its content, paraphrased:

(1) Calculus versus concepts. In the past, calculation dominated mathematics. Hilbert's examples are the invention of the differential and integral calculus, Weierstrass's function theory understood as a calculus of power series, Lie's calculus of operations (infinitesimal transformations), and the calculus of invariants. In future, 'operating with concepts' will dominate. Cauchy and Riemann inaugurated this, and it also shows in the work on the foundations of geometry (implicitly Hilbert's own 1899 Grundlagen der Geometrie).

(2) Quantity reduced to quality. The modern theory of the real numbers (Dedekind cuts, Cantor, or Hilbert's own 1900 axiomatization of the reals as an ordered field) really reduces the concept of quantity to that of quality. The question 'Is a earlier than b?' (an order question, a < b) is a question of quality. In modern terms: the reals are characterized up to isomorphism as a complete ordered field, so magnitude becomes a matter of order relations and structure.

(3) Rigour is not empty. Concept of number, set and axiomatization are 'no empty delusion' in mathematics; one must practise them. The axiomatization of the concepts of physics (cf. his 6th Paris problem) will later make this clear.

(4) Existence versus computation. Against the oft-heard rule that one should compute everything out (P. Gordan: more than 7 operations cannot be carried out), Hilbert replies that in other areas too the human mind is often content with knowing a task can be carried out. His example is the harvest. The sentence breaks off with 'Voraus...' (perhaps 'Voraussicht' or 'Vorausnahme'). This is Hilbert's familiar defence of existence and finiteness proofs, as in his finite basis theorem of 1888/1890 that drew Gordan's 'Das ist Theologie' remark.

results.what: Programmatic claim that conceptual reasoning (Cauchy, Riemann, foundations of geometry) will replace calculation ('Calcül') as the dominant mode of mathematics.
results.modern_name: Conceptual / structural mathematics versus computational mathematics (the 'Riemannian' principle of thought over calculation)
results.usually_credited_to: Associated with Dirichlet and Riemann; articulated by Hilbert in the Zahlbericht preface (1897) and by Minkowski in his Dirichlet address (1905)

results.what: Remark that the modern theory of real numbers reduces quantity to quality, i.e. to order relations ('is a earlier than b?').
results.modern_name: Order-theoretic / axiomatic characterization of the reals (complete ordered field)
results.usually_credited_to: Dedekind (1872), Cantor; Hilbert's axiom system for the reals (1900)

results.what: Defence of axiomatization of number, set and physics concepts as genuine mathematical practice.
results.modern_name: Axiomatic method; Hilbert's 6th problem (axiomatization of physics)

results.what: Reply to Gordan's demand to compute everything: the mind is often content with knowing that something can be carried out (existence proofs).
results.modern_name: Non-constructive existence proofs (e.g. Hilbert basis theorem versus Gordan's constructive invariant theory)
results.usually_credited_to: Hilbert (1888/1890), with the famous Gordan 'Theologie' anecdote

deep.surprise_reason: These are Hilbert's well-known methodological views: concepts over calculation, the axiomatic method, and existence proofs against Gordan's computational demands. They also appear in the Zahlbericht preface, the Paris lecture and his later talks. The only mildly new details are the specific Gordan quip about '7 operations' and the 'quantity reduced to quality' phrasing, which are colourful but minor.
transcription_corrections: Line 6: the manuscript reads 'Opeririren' (a slip), not 'Operiren'.
The interlinear insertion above 'Begriffe' is uncertain; it may read 'nur' or possibly 'neuen'. 'neuen Begriffe der Physik' would fit the sense better.
The last word is cut off at 'Voraus...' (possibly 'Voraussicht'/'Vorausnahme'); the transcription's 'Vorausn[?]-' is a guess.
'Lies Operationencalcül' carries a diacritic over the final 'u' ('Operationencalcül'), consistent with 'Calcül' elsewhere; this is fine.
The inserted parenthesis reads 'P. Gordan: mehr als 7 Operationen könne man nicht ausführen'; this is confirmed.
